title: Dhamaal 4 Crosses ₹190 Crore Worldwide, Nears Ajay Devgn's Top-Eight Club
excerpt: The Indra Kumar-directed adventure comedy has earned ₹190.41 crore gross worldwide in 13 days, placing it as Ajay Devgn's ninth highest-grossing film of all time.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 has grossed ₹190.41 crore worldwide in 13 days.
  • The film is Ajay Devgn's ninth highest-grossing film, surpassing Bol Bachchan.
  • It aims to surpass ₹201 crore from Singham Returns by the end of its third weekend.
  • Despite mixed reviews, family audiences have kept the film's collections steady.

Dhamaal 4, the fourth installment in Indra Kumar's slapstick comedy franchise, has crossed the ₹190 crore worldwide gross mark in its second week of theatrical release. The adventure comedy starring Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, and Jaaved Jaaferi earned ₹190.41 crore gross worldwide by Day 13, according to box office tracker Koimoi.

Second-Week Numbers Hold Steady

The film's domestic performance stands at ₹141.28 crore net (approximately ₹166.71 crore gross) through 13 days. At the overseas box office, Dhamaal 4 has accumulated ₹23.7 crore gross, making it the eighth highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2026 in international markets. The overseas haul puts it within striking distance of Shahid Kapoor's O'Romeo, which earned ₹24.75 crore internationally.

"Franchise's Strongest Opening Week Dhamaal 4 recorded ₹96 crore net in its first week at the domestic box office, according to Bollywood Life's day-wise tracking."

Day-wise collections show the expected weekday slowdown after a strong second weekend. The film earned ₹11.71 crore net on Day 9 (Saturday) and ₹13.8 crore on Day 10 (Sunday), before dropping to ₹3.31 crore on Monday and ₹4.42 crore on Tuesday. The second week has been marked by increased competition from Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which claimed most IMAX and premium large-format screens from Day 8 onward. Dhamaal 4 retained roughly 45 percent of its screen count heading into its second Friday, according to Sacnilk.

Climbing Ajay Devgn's All-Time Rankings

The ₹190 crore milestone places Dhamaal 4 as Ajay Devgn's ninth highest-grossing film at the worldwide box office. It has already overtaken Bol Bachchan (₹165.68 crore) and Golmaal 3 (₹169.09 crore). Its next target is Singham Returns, which closed its theatrical run at ₹201 crore.

Devgn's top five films globally remain Singham Again (₹402.26 crore), Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior (₹364.81 crore), Drishyam 2 (₹339.89 crore), Golmaal Again (₹310.67 crore), and Raid 2 (₹242.57 crore). The franchise's own predecessor, Total Dhamaal, sits at sixth with ₹223.36 crore.

Franchise's Strongest Opening Week

Dhamaal 4 recorded ₹96 crore net in its first week at the domestic box office, according to Bollywood Life's day-wise tracking. That figure surpasses Total Dhamaal's ₹94.55 crore opening-week record, making it the strongest first-week performance in franchise history. The opening weekend alone delivered ₹64.35 crore net domestically, according to Bollywood Hungama, with the Sunday peak of ₹28.15 crore marking the film's single-day high.

The film was produced on a reported budget of ₹200 crore, per NDTV Profit. With worldwide gross at ₹190 crore, it has not yet recovered its production costs at the box office alone, though ancillary revenue from satellite, digital, and music rights typically factors into overall profitability for big-budget franchise films.

Critics Divided, Audiences Steady

Dhamaal 4 has a 20 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 reviews, with an average score of 3.7 out of 10. Bollywood Hungama offered a relatively positive 3 out of 5 stars, calling it "a decent, clean entertainer that should largely appeal to families and kids." NDTV's Saibal Chatterjee was less generous at 2 out of 5, writing that "nothing that Dhamaal 4 throws up stays afloat long enough to give the audience anything to crack up over."

Despite the critical reception, family audiences have kept the film commercially viable. The franchise's core appeal — broad slapstick humor, ensemble chemistry, and the Dhamaal brand name built since 2007 — continues to draw ticket buyers across mass and single-screen circuits. A sequel, Dhamaal 5, was teased in the film's climax, confirming the franchise will continue.

The Road to ₹200 Crore

Trade analysts project Dhamaal 4 will cross ₹200 crore worldwide gross before the end of its third weekend, which begins July 24. That milestone would make it Devgn's ninth film to enter the ₹200 crore club. The third weekend's performance will depend on how well it holds screens against The Odyssey and any new releases entering the market.
